post.caption: Red diamonds almost never get this big. The Moussaieff Red weighs 5.11 carats and was cut from a rough crystal of 13.9 carats found in Brazil. William Goldberg's New York workshop cut it as a triangle, and its first name was the Red Shield. London jewelers Moussaieff bought it and renamed it. GIA graded its color Fancy Red, with no other hue, and it was the largest fancy red that lab had graded. In 2003 it starred in a Smithsonian show, The Splendor of Diamonds, beside the Millennium Star. Photo: Seth Lemmons, CC BY 2.0
